resources.string: Let the AI control the phone
The AI assistant can read the screen, tap, swipe, type and open apps. Every action asks for your approval by default.
The accessibility service is off. Tap to turn it on.
Shizuku is not running or not authorized. Tap to authorize.
Root control has not been confirmed. Tap to review the risks.

Lets the AIDE+ AI assistant read the screen, tap, swipe and type when you ask it to operate your phone. It reads the current window only while an AI phone tool runs (each run asks for your approval by default) and stores nothing.

In the system Accessibility settings, open “AIDE+ AI phone control” (under downloaded or installed apps) and turn it on.\n\nIf Android says the setting is restricted, open the AIDE+ app info page, use the ⋮ menu → “Allow restricted settings”, then try again.
Shizuku is not running. Start Shizuku first, then come back to authorize.

With root, the AI runs input and uiautomator commands as the superuser. Every phone tool still asks you before it runs, but if you switch these tools to automatic, one wrong decision by the model can tap anything, change system settings, send messages or delete data — and root bypasses the protections Android normally applies.\n\nOnly enable this on a device you control, keep the phone tools on “confirm every time”, and watch what the AI does. You can turn it off here at any time.

This acts on the whole phone, not just the project: it can tap, type and open apps anywhere. Check the screen and the target before allowing; never allow payments, transfers, security changes or messages you did not ask for.
